entry.content: eval_chart_transform: description +Cached values are already scaled: scale 3 means non-exempt metrics are in thousands; scale 0 means units. Percentages (75 means 75%), FTEs and other scale-exempt metrics retain their units. Do not scale again; y_scale is forced to 0. For multiple sources, inspect each scale and format; re-query same-unit series at a common scale, and use separately labelled axes for different units (line/bar/area) or separate charts. Conflicting nonempty caption scale labels are omitted; unlabelled sources leave other labels intact. Set axis unit labels explicitly. export_dataset: description -cached +previously returned -query; returns +query. Use this for standard Excel exports of reports already shown, rather than rebuilding their JSON with Python. Financial XLSX uses shared server formatting and retains source/region metadata for add-in conversion. Returns -file and download link. +file/download link; an expired snapshot requires a fresh authorized query, whose values may change.

entry.content: company-search: description, inputSchema +without max_cost_usd, -2 +1 +Such a search stops once it costs more than the companies it found pay for (completion_reason cost_limit, coverage_limited: true). Search budget: with max_cost_usd the whole budget is reserved, and the search goes on until it delivers count or spends the budget. Its search effort is billed where the companies delivered do not cover it, up to the budget, even when it finds few companies or none; the unused part is returned. Set max_cost_usd only when the user agreed to spend that amount, never on your own. Find more: when a search ended before count because a limit parameters: +input.continue_from input.continue_from description: task_id of an earlier Company Search of yours that has ended, to find only new companies: this search leaves out every company that one delivered, held for review, or was told to exclude, as well as your own exclude. Send the same query and filters with count set to the companies still wanted. HTTP 409 while that task has not ended (queued, running, or paused); 404 when it is not your Company Search (a Company Enrich or People Search task_id is refused). -The +Without max_cost_usd the +With continue_from, the companies still wanted. +input. company-search-cancel: description +A Company Search started with max_cost_usd pays for its search effort so far instead when that is more, up to its budget. company-search-status: description -Enrich), +Enrich or a search restricted to the domains its query names, listed as only_domains), -budget +limit -match), +match: the next hint says how to continue it with continue_from), +A search with a budget shows max_cost_usd, and progress.effort_units once it ended (the search effort billed where the companies delivered do not cover it); a continued search shows continue_from. company-search-tasks: description +max_cost_usd and continue_from when a search set them,

entry.title: remote/io.github.genmnz/jean 2026-10-28T132454025984 -> 2026-11-05T145949962255: 272 changed, 2 added
entry.content: activity_cliffs: description -Indices are 0-based. add_notebook_figure: description -It is appended to the entry the user has open (or to the one you name), captioned with the drawing, the tool that drew it and what that tool concludes now, and numbered where it falls, exactly as the Export panel and a chart's own menu do it. Vector drawings stay vector. adopt_trace_calls: description -The signal is untouched — this is the same electropherogram with a second opinion about where the bases are — and every coordinate already on the read is carried across the peaks it sits on, so a trim window, a hand-corrected call and an annotation all follow. Reports what moved and what could not be placed. Use `call_bases_from_trace` instead to ASK what the re-call says without changing the read. align_read: description -Needleman-Wunsch with free end gaps and the IUPAC substitution matrix — SeqTrace's aligner, the same call the trace editor makes, so a pipeline and the panel align a read identically. Leave `reference` unset to align against the record this step runs on. align_sequences: description -`poa` (partial-order, poapy) aligns into a graph, keeps every path a read took and produces its own consensus row — what a pile of reads over one locus wants. `progressive` (biotite) computes Feng-Doolittle distances, clusters them into a guide tree and merges along it under "once a gap, always a gap" — the classic MSA algorithm, what a FAMILY of homologous genes wants, and what a reader coming from Clustal or MUSCLE expects. Wire many upstream `record`/`sequence` outputs into `sequences`, or name library documents. alignment_agreement: description -The reference is a FASTA in this project or a public UCSC assembly, exactly as the panel offers it. There is no threshold and no verdict: a rate in the tens of percent almost always means the reads were aligned to a different assembly than the one asked for, and when the file declares its own reference length the answer says so as a fact rather than as a judgement. alignment_pca: description -Jalview's PCA, with its parameters: gap–gap and gap–residue columns counted, a gap never matching. Needs 4 rows. Wire `alignedSequences` from align_sequences. alignment_redundancy: description -Jalview's definition: a gap matches anything and the pair is compared over the shorter row. Wire `alignedSequences` from align_sequences. alignment_window: description -Wire `reads` into an alignment or a screen the way the pane's own hand-offs do. analyze_melt_curves: description -`plate` (RDML-Python) normalises, derives twice, calls the peaks of -dF/dT and CLASSIFIES them against the target's expected Tm into per-reaction verdicts — one peak in the window is the product, an extra peak is an artifact or a primer dimer, no peak at all is a reaction that did not amplify; it is the only engine that produces a verdict. `vertex` (MBmca diffQ) fits a quadratic near the extremum and reports its vertex, so the Tm is NOT one of the sampled temperatures — the only sub-grid answer. `curve` (qpcR) does no plate normalisation and gives no verdicts, but reports every melting peak w annotate_region: description -Every track answers with its authority, table and retrieval date. Coordinates are 1-based and inclusive, as a person writes chr17:41196312-41277500. antibody_antigen_contacts: description -The antigen is found rather than named: a protein chain with no immunoglobulin variable domain is the thing being bound. Geometric definitions are CREDO's as Arpeggio implements them, graded contact-for-contact against pdbe-arpeggio. `polar` is the hydrogen-bond criterion WITHOUT the donor angle, because a crystal structure carries no hydrogens; it is the superset an angle test would filter, and no angle-checked hydrogen bond is claimed. antibody_canonical_classes: description -Each loop is scored against every cluster of its length by the cluster's position-specific log-odds; the best score above SCALOP's threshold names the class and its median structure (a PDB chain). Graded against the real SCALOP on every heavy, kappa and lambda chain of ANARCI's PDB benchmark. antibody_isotype: description -A domain search says 'a C1-set immunoglobulin domain'; this says which isotype it is. Reads IMGT/GENE-DB's own per-label translations for every species, and is graded against UniProtKB's curated human constant chains and their CH1/hinge/CH2/CH3 regions. antibody_liabilities: description -Every motif is cited to its source. antibody_molecule: description -Each chain keeps its own termini, so this is not the same as pasting the chains end to end. Graded against Biopython ProtParam over every heavy/light pair of ANARCI's PDB benchmark. antibody_position_frequencies: description -Two distributions: IMGT's own germline V and J alleles of a species (one count per reference allele), or a bundled Observed Antibody Space repertoire subset (one count per unique expressed sequence; human naive B cells, Jaffe et al. 2022). Graded against independent pandas counts of ANARCI's germline alignments and of every OAS data unit of the subset. apply_feature_file: description -It REFUSES unless something says the two are in the same coordinate space: if the file names a genome build and the record names the same one it proceeds; if they name different ones it refuses outright; if either is silent it refuses until you pass coordinates_only, which states that you are applying the intervals as positions in this record's own numbering with no genome correspondence checked. Reports what would not fit rather than trimming it. apply_variant_call: description -The REF allele is checked against the sequence first and a mismatch REFUSES naming both: applying a call from a different assembly would produce a construct that looks fine and is wrong. Symbolic and breakend alleles are refused for what they are: they name a rearrangement rather than replacement bases. assemble_index_oligos: description -Audited for the problems that only exist once tag and oligo are concatenated and that no check of the index alone can see — a homopolymer run across the junction, a 5' tetramer recurring as its reverse complement, and an oligo over the synthesis length guideline. assemble_multiple_inserts: description -A complete digest at n sites leaves n arcs and n gaps between them, and every gap has to be filled for the ring to close; the arcs and the inserts go to the same homology assembler the single-insert tool uses, and which insert lands in which gap is read off each construct the homology graph closes rather than guessed. It designs no homology arm: an insert arrives with the ends it has, and a set whose ends do not meet the arcs is the assembler's own refusal. assemble_operon: description -Returns the assembled sequence, its layout, and each gene's achieved strength. assembly_plan_simulate: description -Emits the FINAL construct as a record. The plan is DnaCauldron's own spreadsheet shape — one row per construct, `construct_name, part, part, …`. assess_small_molecule: description -Readings are taken with hydrogens implicit, the form the descriptors and the rules' papers assume. An alert flags a nuisance or reactive substructure; it is not a verdict on activity or toxicity. audit_barcodes: description -This is the question asked of a set inherited from a kit or a previous experiment. audit_cds_annotations: description -A partial end (< or >) is not judged, and a /pseudo CDS carries no flag. Where an annotation ends without a stop it reads on in frame (round the origin of a circular map) to the first stop and says how many codons that adds, whether it runs into another annotated CDS (a fusion annotated in pieces) and the read-through a random backbone of the same composition would give. Extraction and translation match Biopython on all 1,871 CDS of 695 NCBI vector records. auto_annotate: description -Emits an annotated record, so a downstream map or export carries the annotations. back_translate: description -Four rules — the host's most-frequent codon (EMBOSS backtranseq), a draw from the family's real frequency distribution, the IUPAC-degenerate consensus for primers/probes (EMBOSS backtranambig), or DnaChisel's table-free first codon. It does NOT optimize: for restriction-site avoidance, a GC target or repeat removal, follow it with optimize_sequence. bayesian_protein_inference: description -Shared peptides are weighed between their proteins instead of being counted for each. blast_project_sequences: description -Use it to ask which of my constructs, reads or proteins carry this span. Nothing leaves the machine; for public databases use blast_search. blast_search: description -This is the similarity search a methods section cites: it turns an unnamed span into named homologues with E-values, and hands the hits, the tabular report and the job id downstream. The sequence LEAVES THE MACHINE. bootstrap_cq: description -This refits the curve a few hundred times, either by resampling its residuals or by leaving observations out, and reports the spread of everything the fit produces: every model coefficient, the Cq under each definition, the efficiency and the initial fluorescence, each with the quantiles of the iterations rather than a normal approximation, so an asymmetric interval means the estimate genuinely is asymmetric. Reproduces qpcR 1.4.2's `pcrboot`. browse_region: description -Give a gene symbol (resolved through MANE Select, then HGNC) or a locus, 1-based and inclusive. Each lane refuses a window wider than it will read, and says so. build_addgene_deposit: description -The sheet is fetched from Addgene each run, so its columns and choices are current; a value it would refuse is left out and named, and `columns` lists every column with its choices. It WRITES A FILE and sends nothing. build_assembly_report: description -Wire `golden_gate_assemble` or `gibson_assemble`'s `products`, `errors` and `warnings` outputs into it. build_ena_submission: description -Features are checked against the tables ENA's own validator reads, so what Webin-CLI would refuse (an unknown key, a missing mandatory qualifier, a double quote in a value, a duplicate feature) is refused or rewritten here, by name. A description under 10 characters, an entry under 100 bp and a missing study are reported first. It WRITES FILES and sends nothing. build_genbank_submission: description -This is not a GenBank export — GenBank's submission pipeline takes neither a `.gb` nor a plain fasta. Its real work is REFUSING and MIGRATING what GenBank will not accept: twelve feature keys were retired in 2014 in favour of `regulatory` (promoter, terminator and RBS among them, so every plasmid map is affected), a qualifier not on a key's approved list is dropped by name, and an unapproved key is kept as a `misc_feature` carrying its original name. Since December 2024 GenBank has required `collection_date` and `geo_loc_name` on every submission, and both are validated here against the INSDC build_tree: description -Wire it downstream of align_sequences. calculate_power: description -Leave ONE quantity out with `solve_for` and it is solved; everything else is given. Thirteen tests in two families: Cohen's standardized effect sizes (pwr 1.3-0: t one/two-sample/paired and unequal n, one and two proportions by arcsine h, normal mean, correlation, chi-square w, one-way ANOVA f, linear-model f²) and raw units (R's power.t.test from a difference and SD, power.prop.test from two proportions, power.anova.test from variances). Every number is R's, reproduced: the solved value is uniroot's root at R's tolerance, and an unreachable target is refused with R's own message. Returns the calculate_rnaseq_power: description -Leave one of n, cv, effect, alpha and power out (or name it in `solve_for`). Every quantity takes a list, and the answer is the whole grid, so depth against replicates is one call. RNASeqPower 1.52.0 (Hart et al. 2013), reproduced: a negative binomial count with Poisson sequencing noise 1/depth plus biological variance CV². call_bases_from_trace: description -The read can come back a DIFFERENT LENGTH than the file's. This ANSWERS the question; `adopt_trace_calls` is what puts the answer onto the read. call_cq: description -Also reports the two exponential-phase locators (Tichopad take-off, model midpoint), which come back null rather than 0 when a curve has no exponential phase at all. call_mixed_bases_from_trace: description -`mode: het` assumes the two alleles are present in equal amounts, which is the diploid heterozygote case; `mode: mix` assumes nothing about their ratio, for a mixed template, a contaminated read or a pooled sample. The two disagree: on this repo's own corpus they differ on 348 of 5,605 calls. Also returns the ALTERNATIVE calls the search considered and rejected. cancel_research_run: description -Nothing is deleted: a canceled hypothesis stays registered and still counts in e-BH with e 1, because it was registered before any result and dropping it would raise the others' chance of support after the fact. Answered and settled hypotheses cannot be canceled. To stop a run that is advancing in budgeted slices, stop calling resume_research_run; cancel when the pending hypotheses should never run. canonical_tautomer: description -Returns every tautomer, the canonical SMILES, the score and the 0-based atoms (implicit hydrogens, molfile order) a hydrogen moved between. check_assay_decay: description -It answers the question an assay's age raises — the design was made against the genomes available on the day, and the target has drifted under it since — as a RATE per oligo with an exact binomial interval, plus the mismatch count at each position of the oligo, which is the shape a manufacturer's own in-silico inclusivity table takes. IUPAC codes in an oligo are read as the breadth its designers meant, so a position a code covers is never a mismatch; a site overlapping ambiguous bases in a submitted assembly is missing data and leaves that genome out of that oligo's denominator rather than co check_color_balance: description -This is the color question alone; check_index_pool asks it alongside distance, duplicates and hopping for a whole pool. check_golden_gate_parts: description -This is what answers “why will this assembly not work” — an internal site has to be domesticated (silently recoded) before the reaction can be trusted. check_index_pool: description, outputSchema -Takes a pasted list or a vendor kit by id. It CHECKS a pool; design_barcodes builds one. parameters: -swaps +swaps. Absent for a single-index pool, which has no i5 to swap. check_invariants: description -Every verdict names what broke, where, and the remedy. Run this after any design or optimisation step, and stop the chain when `admissible` is false — never report a designed sequence without it. check_manufacturability: description -Every threshold is the vendor's own, read from the vendor's own page with the date it was read, and every finding carries the span it is about so it can be drawn. It reports the limits that are MET as well as the ones exceeded, because a list of failures cannot tell a clean sequence from an unchecked one. It never predicts a synthesis outcome and never rules a sequence out: a vendor publishes what it supports, so being outside a published window is a conversation with the supplier, not a rejection. check_methylation_block: description -The other term of the same reaction question `find_star_sites` answers. It is deliberately per-SITE and not per-enzyme: REBASE says Dam blocks ClaI, and pBR322's single ClaI site carries no overlapping GATC, so the enzyme-level warning does not apply there. An enzyme REBASE has never examined comes back `examined: false`, which is UNTESTED and never a clearance. check_primer_specificity: description -Pairs with no product elsewhere rank first, in the order given, then pairs not checked, then pairs with a named unintended product. Primer sequences and the template LEAVE THE MACHINE; the database is a collection, not an assembled genome, and cannot be filtered by organism. check_rows: description -Fails the pipeline (so everything downstream skips) and names the rows that broke the rule. check_scorpion_stem: description -A Scorpion is a primer carrying a stem-loop probe on a non-amplifiable blocker (Whitcombe 1999), and it reports by the loop finding its target and pulling the stem apart - so the design question is a RELATION between those two structures, not a property of either. Returns both temperatures, their difference, the stem's GC, and a verdict against WHATEVER margin you pass. It does not apply a margin of its own authority: the widely-quoted 5-10 °C figure comes from one design tool's tech note and has no primary citation, so the default is labelled as that rule of thumb and every result says which check_value: description -This is how a pipeline expresses 'only continue if the clone is right'. classify_droplets: description -`grid` applies eight fixed thresholds: reproducible and auditable, the only one that does not move when the data does, and the only one that needs someone to have chosen the numbers. `kmeans` clusters both channels at once and names the clusters by where they sit, so it adapts to the well, and it CANNOT abstain because k-means partitions everything. `knn` classifies against a well you have already labelled and abstains into `Rain` when the neighbour vote is weaker than a floor you set, so it is the only one that can decline per droplet. They disagree on the droplets between the populations, a classify_grammar_part: description -Reads the record's own annotations, which is what lets an assembled transcription unit be recognised by its backbone half, and what lets a Level-0 module whose own backbone carries an extra site for the release enzyme be told from that backbone. Configured entry vectors are a Parts Bin concept and are NOT available here, so a TU sitting in a named acceptor is reported by its overhangs rather than by that acceptor's name. cluster_molecules: description -Indices are 0-based. codon_optimality: description -Where CAI scores how CLOSE each codon is to its family's best, Fop scores only whether it IS one of the best, which makes it comparable across genes of different amino-acid composition. Name a table this project holds in `table`, or one of the bundled hosts in `host`. codon_table_fetch: description -NCBI builds the table by counting codons in the annotated CDS of a RefSeq assembly (the same counting the Codon Usage panel does, with the assembly and CDS count in the provenance); the Kazusa mirror serves a published table for an organism the mirror covers. The table LEAVES NOTHING but takes a network round-trip. Hand the saved name to `codon_usage_analysis` or `codon_optimality` in `table`. codon_usage_distance: description -Every other codon score grades one sequence against a reference TABLE; this one grades two sequences against each other, so it stays available for an organism no authority covers. Answers 'does the gene I inserted use codons like the rest of this construct'. compare_antibodies: description -The alignment is abnumber's `Chain.align`, graded against it over every chain of ANARCI's PDB benchmark; the properties against Biopython ProtParam. compare_constructions: description -Works across formats: a build received as a SnapGene binary and the same build received as an OpenCloning strategy align, because each step's identity is derived from the reaction and its parameters rather than assigned. compare_molecules: description -The first molecule is the query. compare_reads_to_reference: description -This is the whole-plate answer that grading reads one at a time cannot give — a variant is accepted only when every covering read agrees, so a single bad call does not become a mutation. Reads arrive as records or bases; the reference is the record this step runs on. compare_trees: description -Two methods disagreeing is a result about the data, so the distance and the shared topology are reported together. consensus_from_traces: description -Returns the consensus, how many positions are ambiguous, and how many the consensus's own trimming stage cut from the ends. convert_mass_moles: description -The weight is the open record's own, computed from its sequence (both strands of a double-stranded record under its topology, a protein from its residues), or one you give. copy_number_allele_split: description -OncoScan results state a split when the aberrant-cell fraction was determined; the tool says why when a file states none. copy_number_compare: description -Kind is part of the match, so a gain in one sample and a loss in the other at one locus are reported as two unshared calls rather than as agreement. Chromosomes only one file indexes are listed apart and are NOT reported as differences: nothing about them was compared. NO OVERLAP THRESHOLD IS APPLIED — every pair comes back with its numbers, and which agreement counts as agreement is a laboratory's judgement. copy_number_findings: description -Reads the file's own CNState and LOH columns and infers nothing — for a second opinion computed from the log2 ratios, use copy_number_segment. A chromosome that was read and carries nothing is reported as clean, which is a different answer from one that could not be read. NO GENOME BUILD IS ASSUMED: positions are the file's own. copy_number_loh: description -Answers where a sample has lost one parental haplotype, including where copy number is normal. Needs a container that states genotype calls — an OncoScan OSCHP does; a CytoScan CYCHP states the set with no rows, and this says so rather than answering empty. copy_number_mosaicism: description -A mosaic event is present in only some of the sample's cells, so its log2 ratio sits between the levels a clonal change would produce. Every segment comes back with the class it was assigned (±0.3, ±0.5, ±0.7, ±1.0), the fraction that class is NAMED for, its confidence, and whether the method CALLED it as mosaic — a whole-copy change of exactly ±1.0 is clonal and is reported with call 0, which is the vendor's own test. The mixture values are class labels, not measured cell fractions: there is no published method for this estimate and no independent implementation to grade it against, so it is copy_number_read: description -Values the analysis left undefined are counted and reported, never plotted as zero. NO GENOME BUILD IS ASSUMED: positions are the file's own, because these files name an annotation release and not an assembly. copy_number_regions: description -Regions come from ClinGen's dosage-sensitivity curation, cached with its retrieval date — a loss is reported against the region's haploinsufficiency score and a gain against its triplosensitivity score, and no score is claimed for LOH or mosaic events, which change no copy number. NO THRESHOLD IS APPLIED: every overlap is reported with its numbers and which calls are worth reporting is a laboratory's judgement. Regions ClinGen has not placed on this build are listed separately and are NOT reported as clean. copy_number_segment: description -The HMM lays a copy-number model over the log2 ratios and calls a state per segment; circular binary segmentation finds where the mean changes with no model of what a gain looks like, by permutation test; piecewise constant fitting picks the piecewise-constant curve minimizing squared error plus a penalty per jump, with no test and no seed; PELT minimizes the same shape of objective exactly and prices a boundary with an information criterion rather than a tuned constant, so its segment count follows from a model-selection rule. Every parameter and every default is the canvas's own. NO GENOME copy_number_somatic: description -OncoScan CNV Plus states this table; CytoScan and SNP 6.0 results do not, and the tool says so rather than answering empty. crispr_analyze_screen: description -This is the other end of a screen from the pool designer — it reads what came back rather than deciding what to order. The estimator is BAGEL2 (Kim & Hart 2021), reproduced byte-for-byte against upstream, so a gene's Bayes factor here is the number BAGEL2 prints for the same counts. It is a COMPARISON against two reference gene sets, not an absolute fitness measure, and it reports how many of those reference genes the library actually carries, because a screen whose gene symbols do not match the reference sets trains on almost nothing and still returns a ranking. MAGeCK's alpha-RRA and drugZ crispr_design_guides: description -Nuclease list comes from the real nuclease registry. crispr_design_library: description -A spacer that serves two overlapping targets takes ONE well, and every candidate a filter held back is counted by reason, so a short pool says which rule shortened it. It designs a library; it does not analyse one. No recommended representation, MOI or read depth is embedded — the screen-scale arithmetic is in the editor panel, where the numbers are the user's. crispr_quantify_edits: description -Synthego ICE: the CONTROL trace gives the unedited sequence, the EDITED trace is decomposed into a mixture of proposed indels around each guide's cut, and the abundances are fitted. Answers the question a screen cannot: not whether a guide is good, but what it actually did to these cells. crispr_score_deephf: description -It is not a z-score and not comparable with Rule Set 3 — the two answer different questions and must never be averaged or ranked together. Takes 23-nt protospacers (20-nt spacer + NGG PAM), which is what `crispr_design_guides` produces; a guide whose PAM is not canonical NGG comes back null rather than extrapolated, because the model was trained on NGG only. THE WEIGHTS DOWNLOAD ON FIRST USE, 3-5 MB per model, and scoring is slow by construction: each guide is folded twice, once with the 79-nt tracrRNA scaffold, before the network sees it. crispr_score_deepspcas9: description -It is a third quantity, not a second opinion: Rule Set 3 is a z-score across a screen and DeepHF is an efficiency in [0, 1], so none of the three may be averaged or ranked together. Takes the 30-nt CONTEXT the model reads whole (4 nt + 20-nt spacer + 3-nt PAM + 3 nt), which is what `crispr_design_guides` reports as `context30`; a 23-nt protospacer is not enough and comes back null rather than padded. Unlike DeepHF it does NOT require a canonical NGG PAM, because its training library was not NGG-only. The output is the network's own linear value and is left unclipped, so a context it scores be decompose_r_groups: description -Indices are 0-based. delta_blast_smart: description -Searches the open record's coding sequences unless `subjects` gives FASTA. NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0's algorithms, checked against the deltablast program on every bundled protein. Nothing is sent anywhere. describe_discovery_corpus: description -Runs no test and returns no statistic, so hypotheses proposed from it are proposed before any result is seen (POPPER's metadata-only design step). Use it before run_discovery_programme. describe_project: description -Over the API or MCP it describes the files sent as _files; in the app it describes the open project. design_bisulfite_primers: description -BSP primers avoid CpGs so they amplify regardless of methylation state; MSP primers sit ON CpGs so they discriminate. Also reports the CpG islands (EMBOSS cpgplot) the assay should target. design_codehop: description -Each primer is a 3' DEGENERATE core over a few conserved residues fused to a 5' non-degenerate consensus clamp, back-translated through a codon-usage table. A different algorithm from the degenerate designer, not a variant of it. design_combinatorial_library: description -The member set is the Cartesian product of the bins — one part per slot — pruned by design rules, and each surviving member is assembled by the SAME end-homology (Gibson/NEBuilder/In-Fusion) or plain-concatenation engine the single-construct tools use, so a member's construct is identical to assembling its parts on their own. It builds no second assembler; combinatorial Golden Gate lives in the grammar-assembly panel. Every pruned member is kept in the answer with the rule that removed it. design_degenerate_primers: description -A faithful port of DegePrime (Hugerth et al. 2014). Wire an upstream align_sequences `rows` output straight in, or paste an aligned FASTA. design_expression_variants: description -It returns the comparison rather than one answer, because the strategies disagree about what limits expression and the researcher picks. Refuses a frame-shifted CDS, an internal stop or a missing host table rather than optimising nonsense. design_free_codes: description -Or prune a set you already own down to a valid FREE code, and see which members' decode spheres collided. This is a different construction from design_barcodes' distance-based search, and answers a different question: a Levenshtein-distance set corrects indels between two barcodes, a FREE code corrects them in the read. design_fusion_site_primers: description -This is how a sequence that is not yet a Golden Gate part becomes one, and it is the other half of check_golden_gate_parts — that says which parts are unusable, this makes one usable. design_gene_fragment_order: description -A fragment outside the product's length range, unnamed, or carrying a non-IUPAC base is refused by name; one outside the product's published GC or homopolymer limits is kept and named, because a vendor publishes what it supports, not what it rejects. It WRITES A FILE and sends nothing: no account, no key, no network call. design_genetic_circuit: description -The gate parameters are MEASURED, from the published libraries, with the host and growth conditions they were measured under reported alongside — never estimated here. design_gibson_primers: description -This is the step that turns a planned assembly into oligos you can order. design_hcr_probes: description -Each stage reports how many tiles it kept. design_ish_probes: description -Merges OligoMiner's tiling, its trained specificity model and its k-mer filter with iFISH's probe-set selection; each stage reports what it removed and why. design_knockout_package: description -Two donor modes: by default the arms sit on the cut (a point insertion — the target's own sequence is kept on both sides), and with `replace_target` the arms flank the whole target and it is deleted, which is the mode for replacing one CDS with another (an empty insert then deletes the target cleanly). It refuses rather than guessing: no PAM in the target, arms that run off a linear molecule, a screening amplicon that cannot clear the arms, or a non-DNA insert; and in the default mode it WARNS when an insert lands inside the target, because that is a fusion rather than a replacement. Arm leng design_lamp_primers: description -Not a pair: LAMP needs six binding regions in the published order and the distances BETWEEN them are as much of the design as the oligos. Each set comes back with the arithmetic behind its rank. design_merfish_probes: description -Each stage reports how many it kept. design_multisite_primers: description -A design/write. design_mutagenesis_primers: description -A design/write. design_oligo_plate_order: description -A plate order is addressed BY WELL, which a flat tube list cannot express — so this is the shape an oligo set actually gets ordered in once it outgrows a handful of tubes. With `mixed`, a forward and a reverse share one well, which is what the supplier's doubled mix-plate layouts encode. It WRITES A FILE and sends nothing: no account, no key, no network call. design_overhang_set: description -The counterpart to score_overhang_fidelity: that grades a set you already have, this proposes one. The search is greedy-plus-steepest-ascent over the same golden-validated objective: real measured data, a heuristic path, no claim of finding the optimum. design_padlock_probes: description -Without BLAST results it returns the targets to search, and says the junction check has not been run. design_primer_pairs: description -With `task: existing`, supply one primer and it designs the mate. Emits the top pair so a downstream pcr_amplify runs on it. For a sequencing walk use design_sequencing_primers; for pydna's single-pair designer use design_primers. design_primers: description -Emits both primers so a downstream pcr_amplify runs on them — the design→PCR→gel loop. design_saturation_primers: description -Every Tm is Biopython's `Tm_NN` over the Allawi & SantaLucia 1997 nearest-neighbour table (`DNA_NN3`, upstream's own), under the salt correction and buffer below. A design/write. design_sequencing_primers: description -This is the 'how do I read all 6 kb of this construct' question, which a single pair does not answer. Read length and dead zone default to a named facility's published figures (MSU RTSF, ABI 3730XL) rather than to round numbers. design_split_sites: description -Where design_overhang_set proposes junctions for parts you already have, this fragments a sequence you are about to order: it searches every legal arrangement of fragments in your length window and ranks them by the measured ligation efficiency and fidelity of the overhangs each arrangement produces. Ported from OOGGA (Mukundan & Madhusudhan 2025) and scored against the same Potapov 2018 T4 ligase data the fidelity tools use. design_xenium_probes: description -Without BLAST results it returns the targets to search and says the off-target check has not been run. detect_trace_indel: description -This is not mixed-base calling — that asks whether two BASES sit at one position and is blind to a length difference. Emits where the split starts, how long it is, and the two allele sequences the trace deconvolves into, so a pipeline can gate on the answer or carry either allele onward. differential_expression: description -DESeq2 (Love, Huber & Anders 2014): median-of-ratios size factors, negative-binomial GLM with empirical-Bayes shrunken dispersions, Wald or likelihood-ratio test, Cook's-distance outlier handling, independent filtering, optional LFC shrinkage. edgeR quasi-likelihood (Chen et al. 2025): filterByExpr, TMM normalization, a negative-binomial GLM with bias-adjusted QL dispersions squeezed toward an abundance trend, QL F-test. limma-voom (Law et al. 2014): filterByExpr, TMM, log-CPM with mean-variance precision weights, weighted linear models, moderated t. Takes a gene-by-sample count table and a s digest_fragments: description -Emits the selected fragment as a NEW record, so a downstream gel/map/ORF runs on that fragment — the digest→assembly hand-off. digest_reaction_conditions: description -One call is one tube: enzymes that need different temperatures or have no common buffer come back with `singleTube: false`. Needs no open record. discover_annotation_contradictions: description -Each feature backed by experiment (evidence code ECO:0000269) is scored to say what a confirmed feature looks like to the predictor; every other feature, annotated from similarity, sequence analysis or a rule, is ranked among those scores, and its conformal p-value (1 + experimental features scoring at or below it) / (experimental + 1) is corrected across all of them. Signal, by either predictor: von Heijne's weight-matrix score (EMBOSS sigcleave) of the cleavage site UniProt annotates, or DeepSig's probability that the protein carries a signal peptide at all (its eukaryotic network ensemble, discover_codon_outliers: description -Records from different files are different genomes: each is scored against its own file's usage, and the false discovery rate is controlled once across every gene of every genome. Each gene gets Karlin's B and Supek & Vlahoviček's MILC against the pooled usage of the genes, and a G-test of its codon choice within each amino acid against that usage (χ², degrees of freedom from the amino acids it uses). Outliers are typically highly expressed genes (ribosomal proteins are the most deviant class), genes of unusual composition, and some of foreign origin; an outlier is NOT evidence of horizontal discover_flag_rates: description -Every map of a few kilobases spells promoters, splice donors and repeats, so a raw hit count measures length and composition; here each map's own extreme (its most negative promoter ΔG, its highest MaxEntScan donor and acceptor score, its longest homopolymer, tandem repeat, repeated stretch and hairpin arm) is scored against k-let-preserving shuffles of that same map, and the false discovery rate is controlled across the corpus within each statistic. No statistic uses a threshold: none of the three models publishes one, and a vendor's repeat limit is a product's capability, which `check_manuf discover_gene_tree_discordance: description -For every gene the species tree and each of its nearest-neighbour rearrangements (two per internal branch) is fitted by maximum likelihood under GTR + Γ (rates, base frequencies and shape fitted on the species tree, branch lengths refitted on each rearrangement), and the Shimodaira–Hasegawa test asks whether the species tree is significantly worse than the best of them; the false discovery rate is controlled across genes. A rejection says the gene fits another tree better: incomplete lineage sorting does that to a share of genes among closely spaced species, and so do hidden paralogy, alignme discover_reference_concordance: description -Each condition (the Group column of a long-format Cq table) is ranked by geNorm on its own samples; the conditions are then the blocks of a Friedman test and Kendall's W says how far they agree (0 independent orders, 1 the same order everywhere), with an asymptotic χ² p and a Monte Carlo p from shuffling each condition's ranks. Returns every gene's rank in every condition, its mean rank (the meta-ranking) and its best and worst. geNorm cannot order its two most stable genes, so they share rank 1.5 in every condition. Use `rank_reference_genes` for one condition's ranking by all four algorithm discover_reference_stability: description -Each candidate's standard deviation of log2(TPM + pseudocount) across the chosen tissues is ranked among the genes nearest it in mean expression (1,000 by default, from the 19,107 protein-coding genes GTEx measures), giving one p for 'more variable than its peers' and one for 'steadier', each corrected across the candidates. The four rankers the field runs (geNorm M, NormFinder, BestKeeper, comparative ΔCt, and RefFinder's consensus) also order the candidates against each other, reading the tissues as samples. A ranker always finds a most stable gene; the null says whether any candidate is st discover_site_avoidance: description -Avoidance is evidence of the restriction–modification systems a lineage has lived with, and a site a design can rely on being rare. Three nulls: base composition (order-0, Poisson); k-let-preserving shuffles (uShuffle), which holds dinucleotide skews such as CpG depletion in the null rather than reporting them as findings; and R'MES's maximal-order Markov model, the standard in published avoidance analyses, which judges a site of length k against the record's own (k−1)-mers so only what those cannot explain is reported. discover_target_validation: description -Under the null that G is exchangeable with any gene the tables score, G's p in each table is the share of genes scoring at or beyond it; each p is calibrated to the e-value κ·p^(κ−1), the e-values are multiplied in the order given, and the hypothesis passes when the product exceeds 1/α. The product is a valid e-value only when the tests are independent under the null, so the run also reports the joint p: the product's own share among every gene's product, valid whatever the tables' dependence. Returns every test's score, rank, p, e and running product, the test after which the product first c discover_tree_incongruence: description -Each locus is one aligned FASTA file (or a set of wired alignment rows) over the same taxa, named alike in every file. D is the extra parsimony steps one shared tree costs over each locus's own tree; the null deals the same columns into parts of the same sizes at random. One global test over every locus, and one per locus against all the others combined, with the false discovery rate controlled across loci. A locus that recombined or was transferred costs steps when forced onto the others' tree, but so does a locus evolving at a different rate (Darlu & Lecointre 2002), so a call is a candidat domesticate_part: description -Only occurrences the given CDS covers can be fixed this way; any outside it are reported untouched rather than skipped quietly, because a site in a promoter needs a different answer. dot_plot: description -Three real engines: exact k-mer (FlexiDot/dottup), windowed identity (seqinr) and windowed substitution-matrix scoring (EMBOSS dotmatcher), which answer different questions. dot_plot_grid: description -Answers a different question from `dot_plot`, which compares exactly two: this one ranks which members share material and how much. Wire many upstream record/sequence outputs into `sequences`, or name library documents. draw_alignment: description -Wire `alignedSequences` from align_sequences. Name the window around whatever you are asking about — a variable site, a motif, a gap — because a 2,000-column alignment drawn at once shows nothing. draw_gel: description -The same plate the gel panels draw, so the figure and the rail put every fragment in the same place. Wire `fragments` from a digest or `lengths` from an assembly into `lanes`. A fragment the calibrating curve cannot place is COUNTED in `offScale`, never drawn at the well. draw_trace: description -The same geometry the Chromatogram tab draws with, so the figure and the tab put every peak in the same place. Name the window around whatever you are asking about — a mutation site, a trim bound, an ambiguous call — because a whole 1,000-base read drawn at once shows nothing. draw_tree: description -The same layout the phylogeny panel draws with, so the figure and the panel place every node identically. Wire `newick` from build_tree or edit_tree. ebi_align: description -These are the reference implementations a methods section names, so a local alignment can be checked against the tool the field actually cites. The sequences LEAVE THE MACHINE. enumerate_protonation_states: description -Reproduces Dimorphite-DL 2.1.0, including that it neutralizes charged groups first and keeps only the part it neutralized. enumerate_reaction: description -Pick one of 94 library reactions (the 58 robust organic reactions of Hartenfeller et al. 2011 and 36 click-chemistry reactions, as AutoGrow4 encodes them) or pass your own SMARTS. Each product is sanitised; a product set is kept only when every product in it sanitises. Indices are 0-based. enzyme_collection: description -Names the collection, says which of its enzymes the cut catalog can resolve and which it cannot, and — when a record is open — how many times each one cuts it. Left unnamed it answers for the collection that is currently active, and says that is what it did. estimate_effect_size: description -A column can be subtracted row by row first (a reference gene's Ct, giving delta-Ct). Returns the `design` calculate_power takes: Cohen's d for the `t` test, the raw difference and SD for `t_raw`. export_construction_record: description -This is the Export tab of the History & Provenance panel (the same seven writers), refusing the same formats that source cannot produce. export_map_svg: description -Give it enzymes to draw the restriction sites. The linear layout can draw both strands' bases and a window of the record (start/end), which is the sequence view as a figure. export_trace: description -Reports what the chosen target DROPPED — a read written as FASTA loses its annotations, and every target but FASTQ loses the per-base quality — because those losses are invisible in the file itself. Trims the ends first when asked, by the same three methods the Trim section offers, so a graph does not need a separate step to write a trimmed read. export_tree: description -Newick loses annotations the richer formats carry, which is why the conversion is a step you choose rather than something done silently on export. fastq_qc: description -The numbers are FastQC 0.13.0's, checked against the real program, including its quirks: a read's mean quality is the integer mean of its characters, GC is counted on the read cut to a whole 100 (or 1,000) bases, duplication is counted on the first 50 bases, and an adapter found at a position counts at every position after it, so the curve is cumulative. FastQC does not detect the encoding: Phred+33 unless you say 64. It does not trim or filter anything. fetch_article: description -This is how a pipeline reads a paper rather than its abstract; pass the Markdown to find_accessions for the records it names. Only Europe PMC's open-access subset is served, and an article outside it is refused with Europe PMC's own reason. fetch_clinvar_vcf: description -The ID column is the ClinVar Variation ID and INFO carries ClinVar's own CLNSIG, CLNREVSTAT and CLNDN. Use it to put ClinVar's calls for a locus beside your own. fetch_record: description -This is how a pipeline starts from a published sequence rather than from whatever happens to be open. filter_items: description -Emits the kept rows plus how many were dropped, so a downstream gate can act on the count. find_accessions: description -A span is listed only when the archive returns a record with that accession, so a catalog number with an accession's shape is reported as unresolved rather than as a hit. Hand `accessions` to fetch_record. find_assemblies: description -This is how a pipeline starts from a SPECIES rather than from an accession somebody looked up by hand: hand the replicon accession it returns to fetch_record, with a region, to pull a window of that chromosome. Assemblies come back reference-first, so the default pick is the canonical genome. find_linear_motifs: description -Runs ELM's own class patterns ON THIS MACHINE; only the class table is fetched. Applies ELM's context filters: the chance-probability cutoff, family selection, and the globular-domain filter when you pass domains. It does NOT scan for DOMAINS — for those call scan_protein_domains, which submits to EMBL-EBI InterProScan and returns `domains` in exactly the form this tool's `domains` parameter takes. find_primer_snps: description -The template is placed on the UCSC assembly it was cut from, and the placement is proved by comparing the assembly's own sequence with the template; dbSNP 155 is then read over that span from the UCSC Genome Browser, and every primer is reported with the SNPs under it and each one's distance from the 3' end. `excluded` is the SNP spans in the form design_primer_pairs takes, to design around them. The template's sequence does not leave the machine; the assembly, chromosome and span are sent to UCSC. find_star_sites: description -Not cut sites: these need low ionic strength, high pH, Mn²⁺ for Mg²⁺, glycerol, DMSO or some detergents, and are what turns an over-digested reaction into a band pattern that reads as the wrong clone. fold_guide: description -A spacer that base-pairs into the scaffold disrupts the structure Cas9 binds, which is a physical cause of a dead guide rather than a score. Every free energy is a minimum-free-energy fold under the Turner 2004 nearest-neighbour parameters, in kcal/mol, cross-checked against ViennaRNA 2.7.2. fragment_ions: description -Takes ProForma modification tags (a signed mass, a Unimod name, or UNIMOD:accession) on residues and termini. fusion_pcr: description -Emits the fused product as a NEW record. gate_droplets: description -Four steps in a fixed order, each of which needs the previous one's output: a k-means quality check marks wells whose two droplet clusters are not separable, a plate-wide 1%-slice IQR cutoff marks outlier droplets, a two-component Gaussian mixture per well per channel sets the empty-droplet cutoff on the droplets that survive, and the empty fraction inverts through the Poisson zero term to copies/uL. Reports the cluster the droplets landed in and the reason any well was rejected, so a failed well reads as rejected rather than as a concentration. This is the counterpart of `quantify_dpcr`, not gene_set_camera: description -From a count table it fits voom (filterByExpr, TMM, precision weights) and tests the design's coefficient per set (camera); from a ranked statistic it tests that statistic directly (cameraPR). Parametric or rank-based, fixed or per-set estimated correlation, directional or not. Every set is bit-identical to limma in R on filtered pasilla voom and on DESeq2's Wald statistics against every fly GO term. gene_set_enrichment: description -Seeded: a seed reproduces the chosen package's p-values exactly, and every set is bit-identical to that package in R on pasilla's DESeq2 Wald statistics against every fly GO term. gene_set_overrepresentation: description -Reports gene and background ratios, fold enrichment, odds ratio, z-score, p, adjusted p and Storey q-value per set, and which sets pass both cutoffs. Every tested set is bit-identical to enrichit in R on pasilla's DE genes against every fly GO term. generate_conformers: description -Energies in kcal/mol. genotype_pca: description -Validated on 1000 Genomes phase 3 APOL1, all 2,504 samples. get_construction_history: description -This is the build history, not the edit history — for what CHANGED in a document and when, call get_document_history instead. gibson_assemble: description -Emits the first product as a NEW record for downstream nodes. graft_antibody_cdrs: description -The classical humanization route, and the counterpart to humanize_antibody's language model. Reproduces abnumber 0.4.4 over every antibody chain of ANARCI's PDB benchmark. humanize_antibody: description -Reports every mutation, and what the model would change next. Validated against the published PyTorch model on every chain of ANARCI's PDB benchmark. ligate_fragments: description -Each input may be digested by its own enzymes first, which is the digest → ligate hand-off. Emits the first product as a NEW record. ligation_independent_clone: description -Each method's chemistry decides which end survives, and its own authority states the arm it needs. linkage_disequilibrium: description -Validated on every pair of 1000 Genomes phase 3 APOL1 sites. list_databases: description -Call this before searching if unsure which source answers a question. list_experiments: description -Filter by a tag, by collection, or by text in the title and body, so a run can find the entry it is continuing instead of starting a second one about the same experiment. list_research_runs: description -For each run: whether its seal holds, its id, how many hypotheses it registered and how many are supported, not supported or without evidence, how many a resume would run, how many inputs it pins, and what resuming would do. A file whose seal fails is listed as refused with the reason, never dropped. Hand one to research_run_status for its decisions, or to resume_research_run. list_samples: description -This is the headless form of starting a project from a sample: pass an id as a `_subject` or `_files` entry's `sample` and the file is read exactly as the lobby opens it. list_sgrna_scaffolds: description -A scaffold not listed here is one we do not have — the list is what we ship, not what exists. list_traces: description -Wire its `names` into a trace reader's For-each so every read in the project is processed in one pipeline, instead of one node per read. load_record: description -Wire its `record` into any downstream node's $subject. load_trace: description -This is what makes a sequencing read a pipeline input: verify it against a reference, align it, gate on its quality. The trace SIGNAL stays here — a record crosses a wire as bases, and a peak cannot be written as one. lookup_residue_sites: description -Takes a UniProt accession. This is what InterProScan itself does not return — its per-location site array comes back empty — so it is a separate lookup against InterPro, keyed to an entry whose sequence the residue numbers belong to. map_chemical_space: description -Indices are 0-based. map_reaction_atoms: description -Adv. 2021), the most accurate mapper in Lin et al.'s 2022 benchmark of 1,851 curated reactions. Agents join the reactants, each compound is canonicalised and each side sorted before mapping, as RXNMapper does. Returns the reaction SMILES with atom maps and a confidence (the product of each product atom's attention score). A prediction, not a measurement. map_reads: description -This is minimap2 (minimizer seeds, chaining, banded dual-affine extension with inversion detection, MAPQ), ported and checked record for record against the minimap2 2.31 CLI under every `preset` it offers: Illumina short reads (`sr`, the default), RNA-seq across introns (`splice:sr` for short reads, `splice` and `splice:hq` for long RNA or cDNA, which also report every splice junction with its read support), Nanopore, PacBio HiFi and CLR, accurate long reads, Illumina Complete Long Reads, assemblies at three divergence levels, and all-vs-all read overlaps (`ava-pb`, `ava-ont`, where the reads mask_sequence: description -Emits the soft- and hard-masked sequences and the masked intervals, so a pipeline can mask before it searches rather than explaining an empty hit table afterwards. match_part_by_sequence: description -The match is decided by comparing bases, never by a name — so a pipeline can label a fragment it has assembled, or check that a feature really is the part it is called. matched_molecular_pairs: description -Indices are 0-based. melting_temperature: description -Nearest-neighbor (SantaLucia & Hicks 2004 · Allawi & SantaLucia 1997 · Sugimoto 1996 · Breslauer 1986), pydna's dsDNA-binding-domain model, the GC formula, the Wallace rule or NEB, over the salt correction you name, then DMSO and formamide depression under the published model you name. LOCKED NUCLEIC ACID is understood: write the probe as it is ordered, with an L after each locked base (GTCGLAACAGC), and McTigue, Peterson & Kahn's (2004) per-neighbor increments are added to the nearest-neighbor sum. Returns the per-step breakdown the panel shows, so a pipeline can read WHICH coefficient produ miqe_checklist: description -Each answer is Provided (yes or no) and Description/Justification: where in the article when yes, why it is omitted when no; an answer missing that is named. Returns every row, the counts and a TSV under the paper's headers. Run with no answers to read the item ids. Digital PCR has its own checklist, dMIQE 2020. number_antibody: description -Validated against ANARCI 2026.2.13.2 on every chain of its PDB benchmark. optimize_sequence: description -Emits the optimized sequence as a NEW record for downstream nodes. peptide_mass: description -Plain one-letter sequences also take an ion type (b, y, c, z, a, x and their neutral-loss forms); a ProForma peptidoform with modification tags, as masses or Unimod names and accessions (e.g. [TMT6plex]-PEPTM[Oxidation]IDE, M[UNIMOD:35], M[+15.994915]), is weighed monoisotopically with its modifications. pick_first: description -This is how a two-way branch comes back together: wire both arms in, and whichever arm ran is what continues. plan_master_mix: description -Returns each component per reaction and in the mix, the mix to dispense per tube and the total to prepare. plan_next_tools: description, inputSchema -the +its DECLARED -it reads -read — +read, -from one that brings independent evidence. Ask for a `target_type` and it returns the shortest chains of tools that reach it. The hand-offs are the workflow builder's own port graph, so a step it names is a wire the builder would draw. +apart. parameters: -input.independent_only input.independent_only default: false input.independent_only description: keep only steps that read none of the data files the finished run read, so each adds its own evidence. plan_rnaseq_experiment: description -Give `solve_for` n to size the experiment or power to score a design. With `counts` and `dispersions` from a pilot, the power is computed per gene over that real distribution rather than for one idealised gene. Unlike calculate_rnaseq_power this makes no normal approximation, so it is the one to use at small n or low counts. plan_serial_dilution: description -Returns the transfer and diluent volumes for every step, each tube's concentration and cumulative dilution, and what each tube holds after giving its transfer to the next. plan_thermocycler_program: description -The extension rate and the denaturation step come from the product's datasheet and protocol manual; the annealing temperature is yours (from design_primers or pcr_amplify), and anything the manufacturer does not publish comes from the pydna-faithful Taq or Phusion/Q5 preset — the result says which numbers came from where. The check reports the product as a percentage of the vendor's stated maximum, the extension time its rate implies, the substitutions expected per molecule and the fraction of molecules that should be error-free, each finding quoting the specification line it rests on. population_ancestry: description -Single-base records only, as LEA's vcf2geno keeps them. Validated against LEA 3.19.8 on every record and sample of 1000 Genomes phase 3 APOL1. population_fst: description -Every pair when more than two populations are compared. Validated on every site of 1000 Genomes phase 3 APOL1 for the 5 super-populations and 26 populations. population_site_stats: description -Validated on every site and sample of 1000 Genomes phase 3 APOL1 in 32 groups. primer_check: description -The scan is 3'-anchored, so every site it reports matches the oligo's 3' seed exactly and 'no sites' means no seed match rather than a low score. propagate_uncertainty: description -Also reports the derivative per variable and how much of the total variance each one contributes, which is the answer to "which measurement should I make more precisely?". Reproduces qpcR 1.4.2's `propagate`. protein_disorder: description -Negative means predicted unfolded. Reports the whole-protein score, the per-window series, the runs below zero, and the Uversky charge-hydropathy point with the boundary it was judged against. protein_disorder_metapredict: description -Reports a 0–1 score per residue, the IDRs and folded domains its domain caller draws from the smoothed profile, and the percentage of residues at or above the network's threshold. A different question from protein_disorder's FoldIndex, which reads composition alone. protein_membrane_profile: description -A hydrophobicity-based prediction, NOT a trained topology model. protein_profile: description -Returns one value per window with the residue it centres on. protein_signal_peptide: description -Scores a 15-residue window at every position (the 13 residues before the cut plus the first two after) against either the eukaryotic or the prokaryotic training set. Predicts WHERE the cut would fall, not WHETHER the protein is secreted — a high score away from the N-terminus is a look-alike, not a secretion call. protein_topology: description -Reports the labelled path, the runs as residue spans, and the per-residue posterior. Needs the trained model, which the host loads once per session — this refuses by name when it has not been. quantify_base_editing: description -A base editor makes no double-strand break and no indel, so it is invisible to ICE and TIDE: the edit is a C→T or A→G inside the protospacer that shows up only as a second peak under the called base. This models the trace's OWN background from the positions outside the guide, then p-values every base of the guide against it. Emits the significant calls, so a pipeline can gate on whether editing happened and at which position. quantify_dpcr: description -Positives and accepted partitions become lambda = -ln(1 - k/n), lambda becomes copies per uL through the partition volume and the dilution chain, and the confidence interval is carried on the lambda scale under any of eleven published binomial interval methods. Returns the dMIQE-2020 occupancy QC beside every reading, so a well with no positives, or one saturated past 95% occupancy, is reported as such rather than as a number. query_database: description, inputSchema -Nothing here computes science: a connector returns what the authority already published, which is the rule that an authoritative registry outranks anything kept locally. parameters: +default: 10 input.limit rank_next_tests: description -Three grains: `tests` ranks candidate falsification tests against the beliefs a discovery ledger holds, each with the posterior its two outcomes would leave, by gain and separately by gain per unit cost; `measurements` says what n readings of a normal quantity would teach, and how many it takes to reach a target; `trials` says the same for a rate held as a Beta. A gain is what a result would settle whichever way it lands — never evidence that a hypothesis is true, which stays with the ledger's e-values. rank_reference_genes: description -They disagree on real plates, which is the point of running them side by side; the consensus is the geometric mean of the four ranks. Also returns geNorm's pairwise variation V(n/n+1), whose 0.15 cutoff is what says HOW MANY genes to normalise to. rank_strategies: description -It runs them all, keeps the ones that really produce a construct, and reports the rest with the refusal the chemistry itself gave — so 'Golden Gate is the only way to build this, and its overhangs ligate correctly 99.8% of the time' is one step rather than six runs and a spreadsheet. There is deliberately no single 'best' score: combining the criteria needs weights nobody has settled, and the one criterion every published ranking leads with (cost) has no price this app can honestly cache. So the comparison is the answer, and the sort is by whichever criterion you name. rank_tradeoffs: description -Returns each candidate's front (1 = non-dominated), the candidate one front up that beats it, and its crowding distance within its front (how isolated it is, so a short list can be spread along the front). Rows can be filtered first (`em_max>=580, agg=m`), and rows with an empty objective are left out and counted, never ranked last. moocore 0.3.2's pareto_rank and is_nondominated, emoa 0.5-3's and pymoo 0.6.2's crowding distances, reproduced. read_mgf: description -A spectrum it returns is what score_spectrum takes as mz, intensity and precursorCharge. read_mzml: description -An MS/MS spectrum it returns is what score_spectrum takes as mz, intensity and precursorCharge. read_rdml_run: description -This is the step every qPCR analysis starts from. Lists what each run actually holds (amplification curves, melting curves, instrument Cq values, digital-PCR partition counts with the partition volume the file declares) before anything is imported, so a run is chosen on what is in it rather than on its name. Takes the UNCOMPRESSED XML: a `.rdml` archive is a zip, and the tool vocabulary here has no file input. read_sequencing_qc: description -These are the numbers that say whether a disappointing read is the clone's fault or the run's — a base called wrong under 3x coverage is a sequencing problem, not a cloning one. For a coverage table it also measures the track's SHAPE, because a mean has none: a run averaging 200x with one uncovered region reads as excellent. The provider states one number and two shapes — 20x for an accurate consensus, and a large gap or a sudden large increase meaning an assembly issue or a mixture of plasmid species — so the longest stretch under the line and the largest change in level are both measured an read_structure: description -Use it to answer what a structure IS before deciding what to do with it, or to pull a chain's sequence out of a structure so it can be aligned, back-translated or ordered. Reading only: it never writes a structure file and never applies symmetry, so every count it reports is a count of what the file actually holds — for a core CIF that is the asymmetric unit, not the whole cell. read_structure_consensus: description -Reports the base pairs, what each unpaired column is (hairpin, bulge, multifurcation, external, insertion, local end), and per pair the fraction of rows whose two bases form a canonical or GU wobble pair. Use it to check whether a family's published structure is borne out by the sequences, or to pull a pair table out of an alignment for drawing. Reading only, and it REFUSES a Pfam alignment by name: `SS_cons` is two alphabets, and Pfam writes protein DSSP states in the same field, where C/H/E are pseudoknot letters in WUSS — parsing one as the other would invent base pairs for a protein. read_variant_calls: description -Every answer says what it read over and what it filtered on, so a count can never be mistaken for the file's total. A call set too large to read whole opens at its header, and a locus is then the way in rather than an option. recombine: description -Emits the first product as a NEW record for downstream nodes. recompute_trace_quality: description -Keeps the bases; only their quality changes. Reports the read's mean quality, its lowest-scoring base and the four trace parameters that base was scored from, which are the whole input to the quality table. record_composition: description -The nucleic-acid counterpart of `protein_properties`, and the same derivation the editor's Properties panel, its inspector and the alignment inspector all draw (Biopython's mass model; ProtParam for a protein subject). record_experiment: description -The body is markdown and its @plasmid / !action / &gel references are extracted as you write, so an entry made by a run is cross-linked exactly like one you typed — and carries the `automated` tag, so you can always tell which is which. Use it to end a pipeline with a record of itself instead of a reminder to write one. relative_expression: description -Reproduces the `pcr` package's `pcr_ddct`/`pcr_dct`/`pcr_curve`, including its separate-tube and same-tube estimators, which differ in WHEN the subtraction happens and are not a display option. A significance test runs beside the model on request - Welch t-test, the equivalent linear model, the Wilcoxon rank-sum test with R's own exactness rule, or a design-matrix lm for designs the two-group form cannot express - and delta-delta-Ct's equal-efficiency assumption can be checked in the same run. remember_lab_preference: description -Use it when the user says what they use ("we use Q5", "our primers are 20 to 24 nt"). Saved where the user reads and edits it, Settings · Lab; each panel still says when it is showing the lab's choice, and a project can still choose otherwise. Enzyme supplier order is saved in Enzyme Collections, not here. research_run_status: description -Given the corpus, also reports every pinned input whose content changed under the same name, which a resume refuses. resolve_gene_sets: description -Returns GMT text for gene_set_overrepresentation, gene_set_enrichment and gene_set_camera, with the source, release and retrieval date. restore_trace_file_calls: description -The same carry runs in the other direction, so the trim window, the hand-corrected calls and the annotations come back with it rather than being left on indices the file does not have. Not the same as clearing the read's edits, which also discards the trim and the manual calls. restriction_ligate: description -This is the reaction Golden Gate is a special case of, and it is a different chemistry from ligate_fragments, which digests first and then ligates whatever the digest left. Reports how many sites of the FIRST enzyme each product still carries — a finished construct has none. resume_research_run: description -Answered, settled and canceled hypotheses are never run again, so a resumed run reaches the verdicts an uninterrupted one would. With budget_seconds, a long run continues in slices: call again with the returned file until nothing is pending. Returns the updated run file with the same outputs as run_discovery_programme. rps_blast_cdd: description -Returns every domain hit with its hit type (specific, non-specific, superfamily, multi-domain), residue span, E-value, bit score, CDD accession, superfamily cluster and whether the alignment stops short of either end of the model. This is the rpsblast program. Give `protein`, or give `dna` to send its six reading frames as six proteins (per-frame CD-Search: each E-value is for its own frame, which is not rpstblastn; rpstblastn_smart runs rpstblastn itself on this machine). The query leaves the machine for NCBI. rps_blast_smart: description -NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0's algorithms, checked against the rpsblast program on every bundled protein. Nothing is sent anywhere; for all of CDD use rps_blast_cdd, which goes to NCBI. rpstblastn_smart: description -Leave `sequence` empty to search the open record. NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0's algorithms, checked against the rpstblastn program on every bundled GenBank record. Nothing is sent anywhere; for all of CDD use rps_blast_cdd on a translated protein. run_discovery_programme: description -Each registered test then runs once over the corpus, every answering result is attached as a κ-calibrated e-value (evidence from another test, a changed parameter or the same data twice is refused and reported), and e-BH decides over all hypotheses, those without evidence included. Returns the verdicts, the whole ledger as a file that imports into Discovery Expert, every run's input, the refusals, and the literature query each supported hypothesis needs before it may be called new. Pass a previous ledger with posterior beliefs to get the follow-up order by Bayesian surprise, which ranks what run_gel_plate: description -Wire one `run_gel_lane` per lane into `lanes`. The migration model is `@ports/gel`, the same one the Virtual Gel Bench panel draws. save_enzyme_collection: description -Every name is checked against the cut catalog first and an unknown one refuses the whole save by name, because a collection that silently lost two enzymes is worse than one that was never made. An existing collection is never overwritten unless you say so. scaffold_network: description -Every node with the structures that contain it and how many times the network made it, and every edge with RDKit's type. Structures over the cut limit are named and left out. Indices are 0-based. scan_intrinsic_terminators: description -TWO NUMBERS, BOTH LOWER IS STRONGER - how well the hairpin folds and how thymine-rich the tail is - and NEITHER IS A FREE ENERGY: they are costs in this model's own scheme and must not be compared with a promoter's ΔG or a Turner ΔG. This is the question behind a downstream gene in an operon that goes quiet: a cryptic terminator inside an insert stops transcription that was meant to continue. Rho-DEPENDENT termination needs the protein and is not a sequence motif this or any such model can see. Reports every candidate clearing the two published cutoffs; TransTermHP itself lists one per positi scan_motif_sites: description -It is the scan the optimizer's avoid-motif specification counts, so the sites it lists are the ones an optimisation with that motif would remove. Each site carries its log-odds score and where that score falls in the matrix's range. A match is a sequence resemblance to the matrix, not evidence of binding. scan_protein_domains: description -This is the DOMAIN half of the Protein domains panel; for the short linear motifs a profile scan cannot see, use find_linear_motifs, which takes the `domains` this tool emits. The scan runs at EBI, takes minutes, and needs a contact address because EBI requires one. scan_sigma70_promoters: description -THE NUMBER IS A FREE ENERGY AND MORE NEGATIVE IS STRONGER, which is the opposite direction from a score; the transcription rate beside it is the paper's own rate law over that energy. It answers "could RNA polymerase start here", not "does it": nothing here knows about regulators, supercoiling or growth phase. It is E. coli σ70 and says nothing about σ38/σ32/σ54 promoters or about another organism's polymerase. scan_splice_sites: description -Every GT and AG is scored two ways that are NOT on one scale and are never combined: `maxEnt` is strength under Yeo & Burge's published maximum-entropy model, and `typicality` is log-odds against base frequencies MEASURED at the annotated splice sites of Arabidopsis thaliana TAIR10 (Ensembl Plants 63). IT RETURNS NO VERDICT and has no default threshold: neither model publishes a cutoff, so this RANKS candidates and what counts as dangerous is your call, with both numbers in front of you. score_overhang_fidelity: description -It is the number NEB's Ligase Fidelity Viewer reports: the expected fraction of assemblies in which EVERY junction ligated correctly. This is the quantitative counterpart to check_golden_gate_parts: that says whether the parts will be cut, this says whether the pieces will go back together in the right order. Wire golden_gate_assemble's `overhangs` output straight into it. score_rbs: description -This reads an existing 5'UTR — design_rbs writes a new one. score_variant_effect: description -It ranks a saturation library without an assay — and it is a RANKING IN NATS, not a stability measurement: it carries no kcal/mol and is calibrated against nothing. THE MODEL IS DOWNLOADED ON FIRST RUN, 30 MB for the 8M export and 2.6 GB for the 650M one, then cached; a run in a browser with no network to Hugging Face will refuse rather than hang. screen_contamination: description -Reports every match graded Strong/Moderate/Weak plus the short 'suspect origin' stretches NCBI asks to be removed with the vector, and emits both the N-masked sequence and the longest clean region so a pipeline can gate on the result or carry the clean part onward. screen_guides: description -A guide that folds onto its own scaffold is loaded into Cas9 poorly however good its on-target score is, so this is the check that explains a guide with a good score and no activity. screen_molecule_library: description -Returns, per 0-based structure, the rules it breaks and the alerts it trips, and the binned distribution with how many structures fall within the bound. screen_oligo_structure: description -This is primer3's `thal` — the same engine the Tm columns elsewhere use — so a pool can be screened before it is ordered rather than explained after a gel. The 3'-end measures are the ones that matter for a primer-dimer BAND, because only a paired 3' end extends. Works on any oligo: primers, probes, ssODN donors, guides, adapters. search_molecule_library: description -Returns the 0-based indices of the hits and of any structure RDKit could not read. search_off_targets: description -This is specificity against what you searched — it is not a genome-wide score, and it says so rather than inventing one. search_records: description -This is the half of Fetch from database that answers "which record do I want?"; fetch_record answers "give me that one". A source that is down does not fail the search: its error comes back beside the hits the others returned. select_substitution_model: description -Fitting on a shared topology is the point: a model test that also searched topologies would vary two things at once, and a log-likelihood measured on a different tree answers a different question. Wire the winning model into build_tree's `ml_model`. simulate_rnaseq_power: description -Reports power stratified by expression, the FDR actually achieved, true and false calls, and power at other depths; reproducible from its seed, value for value against R. simulate_taqman_curve: description -Ports DYNAMIC (Kreitmann et al., Anal. Chem. 2026, 98(12):9089-9101): thirteen species, four phases per cycle, mass-action annealing integrated as a stiff ODE, with primer-dimer formation and amplicon re-annealing competing for the primers. It is SINGLEPLEX, which is the paper's own stated limit and not an omission here - one target per run, no interassay competition.
