Two things it needs said about their provenance every time they are quoted: the primer-dimer free energy is upstream's NUPACK quantity and primer3's `thal` is explicitly NOT a substitute for it, and the association rate constant size_fragments: description -A fragment run carries no sequence at all — dye channels and a ladder — so this is the node that turns one into numbers a pipeline can act on: allele sizes, a peak table, and the ladder's own measured accuracy beside them. solve_dilution: description -Returns all four, the fold and the diluent volume to add. Refuses a 'dilution' that would raise the concentration, and two concentrations of different dimensions. summarize_rows: description -This is what makes a CROSS-ROW check expressible: `check_rows` can only assert the same thing of every row, so "the largest fragment is at least twice the smallest" needed two summaries and a comparison and had nowhere to come from. Name a `group_field` and it summarizes each group instead of the whole table (the mean product size per template), emitting a table a gate can then check group by group; pick a pairwise operation and it relates two columns of the same rows. survey_off_targets: description -Returns counts and the aggregate specificity per spacer, never the sites themselves, so a few hundred spacers cost a few hundred rows rather than a few hundred thousand. target_decoy_qvalues: description -Supports the +1 and finite-sample corrections of Levitsky et al. 2017. tide_quantify_indels: description -This is a different question from crispr_quantify_edits, not a cheaper version of it: ICE fits a mixture of whole proposed alleles and names them, TIDE fits the control trace shifted by n bases and so reports how much of the population shifted by n, whatever allele carried it. Run both on the same pair when the two disagree about how much was edited — that disagreement is information about the read. trace_raw_signal: description -This separates an instrument problem from an analysis problem — a read whose analyzed trace looks wrong while its raw channels are clean was mis-analyzed, not mis-run, and a baseline spread far above the others names the channel responsible. ABIF only: SCF and ZTR store no raw channels, and this refuses rather than substituting the processed ones. transform_tree: description -Pruning the TREE keeps the branch lengths estimated from the full alignment, which is a different answer from rebuilding without those taxa. tree_taxon_annotations: description -This is the tip data the phylogeny canvas draws as a strip beside the tips, where a value that recurs further down is a group the tree does not keep together. trim_reads: description -This is cutadapt's algorithm: quality trimming is BWA's running-sum rule (not a threshold - a single bad base in a good tail is absorbed, a real decline is not), and the adapter is found by semiglobal alignment allowing errors, so a PARTIAL adapter at the very end of a read is caught where a substring search would miss it. Quality trimming runs FIRST and adapter removal second, which is cutadapt's own order and changes the result when a low-quality tail is also the start of an adapter. THE REPORT ATTRIBUTES EVERY REMOVED BASE TO THE STEP THAT REMOVED IT, because losing 30% of your bases to qu trim_trace: description -Returns the kept interval as 1-based inclusive bounds, and the mean quality of what it KEPT beside the mean of what it DISCARDED — the pair that says whether the trim was worth making, because a trim whose discarded ends score no worse than the bases it left has shortened the read for nothing. validate_gene_trait: description -(1) GTEx v8 expression: either G's co-expression across the 54 tissues with the trait's own gene(s), such as IL2 for IL-2 production, or G's expression in named tissues against its own elsewhere. (2) The GWAS Catalog: how many studies place an association inside G for traits in the named GWAS Catalog categories. Each p is G's rank among the 19,107 protein-coding genes GTEx measures, so it is exact under the null that G is just another gene, with no model of how expression or GWAS hits are distributed. Each p becomes an e-value (κ calibrator), the running product is the evidence, and testing s variant_call_summary: description -Reports what could NOT be counted rather than leaving a zero standing in for it, meaning a file whose genotypes were not parsed, and any genotype naming an allele its record never declares. variant_consequences: description -Each call's most severe consequence is picked by Ensembl's own ranking. A symbolic allele, or a REF the reference does not carry at that position, is reported as not annotated rather than read against the wrong sequence. A CDS naming no /transl_table is read on the standard code, as INSDC specifies. verify_construct: description -Aligns the two, reports every substitution, indel and uncalled position, then maps each onto the design's features and ranks them by Ensembl's published consequence severity — so a pipeline can gate on 'nothing worse than synonymous' rather than on a bare difference count. write_structure_library: description -Written as RDKit's SDWriter, MolToSmiles and MolToCXSmiles write it; a structure RDKit cannot read is left out and its index returned. added describe_tools added read_answer_window

entry.content: assets_by_metric_tool: description, inputSchema +Every response has `values`: one row per asset in ranking order with the ranked metric's value, plus any `value_metrics` asked for (e.g. the price change of each of the top 100 by market cap, in one call). parameters: +input.filters input.filters description: Extra filters on other metrics, combined with AND. The ranking still uses `metric`. Each filter uses the same `from`/`to` window as the ranking. At most 3. Example — the largest assets by market cap whose price fell more than 5%: `{metric: "marketcap_usd", sort: "desc", filters: [{metric: "price_usd", operator: "percent_down", threshold: 5}], ...}` Filters pick from the whole asset universe before ranking. To screen only the current top N (e.g. "which of the top 200 moved less than 1%"), rank without filters and read `value_metrics` instead. input.filt fetch_metric_data_tool: inputSchema parameters: +Unknown slugs are skipped and listed in `invalid_slugs`; the others are still fetched.

entry.content: publish: description, inputSchema +`platformText` ({ twitter: "…", linkedin: "…" }) gives each platform its own caption, as update_scheduled_post takes it (saved on the draft with contentId); unknown arguments are refused (422 unknown_fields). parameters: +input.platformText input.platformText description: Per-platform captions for this post, the same shape, validation and limits as PATCH /api/v2/posts/{id}: { "twitter": "…" } gives X its own caption, null / "" clears one, null clears them all; an over-limit caption is a 422. With contentId they are merged into the item's stored captions and saved on it first (so a later edit, re-book or review uses the same ones); with `content` they apply on top of that text. Platforms without one get the text, auto-fit. Per-platform captions: platform id → the caption that platform gets instead of `text`, e.
